Move the site template to baseline 1.13.0 (#269)

Move the site template of cleanlanguage.ai from baseline 1.11.4 to
1.13.0, after verifying the archive and its SHA256SUMS against the
published digests, which .baseline/pin.toml records.

- Copy the 1.13.0 files: baseline.css with its decrease-only spacing
  tokens and flush download blocks, rail.js with its fragment fix, the
  NodeKeeper palette, the upstream Dancing Script font, the builder and
  the documents. The copy holds only the 9 logos that the pages load.
- Name 1.13.0 in .baseline/site-card.toml, which adds the favicon key
  from which the card builder writes the site's favicon.ico, and in the
  docstring and comments of tools/build-site.py.
- Regenerate the pages so that they load the baseline files with
  ?v=1.13.0, with the sitemap, and add site/favicon.ico.
- Name 1.13.0 and the project names and domain names in the Site
  template entry of NOTICE.md, and the project names and domain names
  on the Licence page.
- Redirect the 22 logo URLs that the copy no longer holds to the logo
  of each one's own project, written by tools/set-release-links.py.
- Narrow check 7 of tools/check-install-page.py: a rule of
  site/_redirects whose source lies under /assets/ passes only when
  its source is an exact path that nothing under site/ occupies, in
  any letter case, and the rule sends that source with the status 301
  to a file under /assets/baseline/logos/ that
  tools/check-baseline-pin.py pins, with no query, fragment or further
  field. Every other rule under /assets/ fails, as before. A line of
  site/_redirects ends only at a line feed and fails when it holds any
  other control character, a line or paragraph separator, a byte order
  mark or whitespace other than the space. A rule whose source, after
  any https:// and host, starts with the segment favicon.ico, which a
  browser may request without a link, fails whatever its destination
  and status.
- Word the refusals that the checks of tools/check-install-page.py
  report, its pass message, docstrings and comments so that each
  claims only what its check proves or, for the refusals that keep
  their words, what holds for every case refused, and word the
  docstrings, comments and expected words of tools/test-install-page.py
  the same way. The gate's exit 3 messages are not reworded; the one
  that says a file it reads does not exist is untrue whenever
  something is at that path that is not a regular file once any link
  is followed (a folder, a FIFO, a socket or a device), and whenever
  the path cannot be examined for a reason other than that nothing is
  there, such as a folder above it that cannot be searched.
- Add site/** to both path lists of .github/workflows/install-page.yml,
  so that check 7 runs on any change under site/.
- Pin the logo list in tools/check-baseline-pin.py and copy only those
  logos and no .ico file in tools/copy-baseline.py, with tests.
- Update the rule pin in tools/install-page-rules.txt, which
  tools/test-install-page.py reads, and the verify page pin of
  tools/test-build-site.py, whose 2 digests change because the page's
  5 ?v= tokens now read 1.13.0.
- Check in tools/test-build-site.py that site/favicon.ico is listed in
  static_files and hashes to the digest that .baseline/SHA256SUMS lists
  for the favicon of the site that .baseline/site-card.toml names,
  reading that file from its bytes, so that its line ended by a
  carriage return or a CRLF fails.
- Run the 2 cases of tools/test-install-page.py that need 2 folders
  whose names differ only in letter case only where the file system of
  the case's scratch folder holds both names, which the test probes
  there, and name each as skipped with its reason elsewhere. Fail any
  other case whose copy holds 2 such names in 1 folder, or a folder
  that the test cannot list, and check the probe, the skip and that
  reading with stand-ins.
- Run every case in run_cases(), which the test checks with stand-ins,
  and fail unless each case and each residual is run, or left unrun
  with a reason, exactly once, and unless a 2nd look at a new scratch
  folder bears out each skip; count only the cases run. Check that 2nd
  look, and main()'s reading of it in case_run_problems(), with
  stand-ins too, and check that main() runs the cases only through
  case_run_problems(), passing it that loop and look itself, and
  binds none of their names and sets no attribute, as those forms
  read in its syntax tree. An edit to main() that runs the cases
  another way, as through globals() or under another name, or an edit
  that changes those functions before that check runs, rests on
  review.
- Add cases for a rule with the status 201, 300, 303, 304, 305, 306,
  307, 308 or 404, or with 0301, 3010, 301.0, +301 or 301! as its
  status, for a placeholder at the start of a segment that is not the
  last, for a placeholder :d, :x or :zz or the splat ** as the whole
  of a segment, and for a splat that ends a segment, each in place of
  part of the path of the font that the install pages load. These
  cases are examples of the contract of check 7: no finite set of
  inputs can show that no weakening of check 7 passes them.
- Hold the code of tools/check-install-page.py in
  tools/test-install-page.py by 2 layers. First, before it runs any
  code of the gate, the test reads the gate's bytes once and stops
  with exit 1 unless their sha256 is GATE_SHA256, a digest written in
  the test, which the gate cannot write; its message names the file
  and both digests, or, where the bytes cannot be read, the file, the
  error and the digest that GATE_SHA256 records. Every load of the
  gate in the test's process compiles and runs exactly those bytes,
  never through the import system, each case runs a copy written
  from them, and the 2 probes that load that copy in a separate
  process make the same check first and compile its bytes too. Until
  a reviewer renews that digest, any change to the gate, a comment
  included, stops the test before any case, whatever route the change
  takes. Second, the reader pin: from the same bytes, by the gate's
  syntax tree and symbol table, the test derives READER_NAMES, which
  are redirect_problems() and each function that a def at the top
  level of the gate binds and that it reads by name, in turn, and
  READER_GLOBALS, the other names of the gate that those functions
  read, and fails unless they are the names written, unless each is
  bound exactly once in the gate, by a statement at its top level,
  unless the loaded gate binds each function to the one that its def
  makes, and unless the sha256 of each name's statement, with any
  docstring left out, and of the text that the test writes for its
  value equals the digest that READER_SHA256 records. That text gives
  plain data by repr(), a pattern by its text and flags, and a module,
  a class or a path by its name, so another module, class or path of
  the same name gives the same digest. Plain data is a str, bytes,
  int, float, bool or None, or a tuple, a list or a dict that holds
  only plain data, each of exactly that type. For any other value, a
  subclass of those types among them, the reader pin fails, naming
  the name, the reviewed gate included, as it does for a value with
  __wrapped__ that a def does not bind, and a check of the test holds
  these refusals. When the gate's digest is renewed, a change to a
  statement that the reader pin holds still fails, by name, until its
  own digest is renewed too. The reader pin follows only names read
  directly: a helper that a pinned function reaches in any other way
  than by reading the name that a def at the gate's top level binds
  is not derived. Examples of that class, not a complete list, are a
  helper reached through an alias, a lambda assigned at the top level,
  functools.partial, a class or getattr(), or through an attribute of
  a module or a path that a pinned name holds. A helper reached
  through the value of a pinned name that the reader pin refuses, such
  as a dict or a list of functions or of classes, a subclass of dict
  or tuple whose own repr() holds no address, or a set of functions,
  is in that class too, but there the test fails closed: the reader
  pin fails on such a gate, the reviewed one included. Nor does the
  reader pin see a rebinding made while the gate loads that leaves
  each pinned statement and the text of each pinned value as they
  were. Examples of that class, not a complete list, are a rebinding
  through globals(), setattr or exec of a builtin, of a module by
  another module of the same name, of a function by a wrapper around
  it, of __file__, of a pinned value by another module, class or path
  of the same name, or of a function of a sibling tool, rebound and
  restored around a call. A reviewer records a new digest of either
  layer only after reading the change. The residuals, stated once:
  1. Renewing a digest accepts whatever the diff holds. A change that
     edits the gate and records the new digests passes. The test then
     guarantees that the bytes of the gate that run are those that a
     reviewer accepted, not that they are right or that no weakening
     of check 7 can pass.
  2. Once the gate's digest is renewed, a change that alters what the
     reader does by a route that the reader pin does not follow
     passes and is held only by review of the gate's diff. Examples,
     not a complete list: the routes above on which the test does not
     fail closed, a rebinding through globals(), setattr or exec when
     the gate runs as a command, the gate's main(), which is not
     pinned, and code at the gate's top level that changes the test's
     values once the bytes are checked.
  3. Code outside the gate is pinned by neither layer and can change
     what the gate or the test does. Examples, not a complete list:
     tools/check-baseline-pin.py, which the gate runs; the 2 sibling
     tools that the test loads in its own process through the import
     system, tools/check-baseline-pin.py and
     tools/check-inline-code.py, where a cached bytecode file of
     either can stand in for its source, though both loads run only
     after the gate's digest is checked; and Python's own modules,
     such as re, held only by the version guard.
  4. An edit to tools/test-install-page.py itself is held only by
     review. An edit that also changes the digests, the check or the
     reader pin passes, as does an edit that makes main() run the
     cases, or read those it left unrun, another way. The test cannot
     hold itself against its own edits.
  5. The residuals of the gate's own guarantee, which its module
     docstring accepts, are unchanged, including how Pages really
     matches :name and a splat across /, which has not been observed
     (an inference, made with no network).
  6. Every edit of the gate, a comment or a docstring included, stops
     the test before any case until the gate's digest is renewed. A
     prose fix of the gate needs no new digest in READER_SHA256, and a
     refactor of the reader needs both.
- Merge main into the branch. Git reported conflicts in
  site-src/site.json and in 5 generated files: site/channels/index.html,
  site/checklist/index.html, site/examples/index.html,
  site/standard/index.html and site/sitemap.xml. site-src/site.json was
  written from its 3 versions and is the branch's file unchanged. Of
  its keys, only the modified dates of the standard, examples, channels
  and checklist pages changed on both sides, and it keeps the branch's
  2026-11-13 on them in place of main's 2026-11-12.
  The 4 pages were regenerated with tools/build-site.py and the sitemap
  with tools/generate-sitemap.py --write, not by hand.
- Merge main again, with pull request 281, which renames the portable
  instructions files to cleanlanguage-instructions and redirects their
  old names. Git reported conflicts in 7 files. The docstring of
  tools/test-release-links.py keeps this branch's pin of the 22 logo
  redirects and main's pin of the closed form of every redirect rule
  and of the old instructions names, and the count of redirect lines
  is 14 + 22. The tests that this branch adds now follow main's 14
  lines before the logo redirects: FIXED_LINES, RELEASE_LINES and the
  line that an appended rule takes, now 37, and a docstring and a
  comment of tools/check-install-page.py that named
  /apple-touch-icon.png as line 10 now name line 14.
  site-src/site.json keeps both sides' static files and main's later
  dates, and the pages and the sitemap were regenerated, not edited by
  hand.
- Merge main again, with pull requests 268 and 279. Pull request 268
  adds a CI gate for pull request texts, tools/check-pr-text.py, with
  its tests and the Pull request text workflow; this branch changes
  none of its 7 files. Pull request 279 licenses the project under
  Apache-2.0. Git reported conflicts in site-src/site.json,
  site/license/index.html and site/sitemap.xml. Of the keys of
  site-src/site.json, only the modified date of the licence page
  changed on both sides, and it keeps main's later 2026-11-18; the
  page and the sitemap were regenerated, not edited by hand. NOTICE.md
  and site-src/pages/license.html, merged without conflict, keep both
  sides' changes. cleanlanguage/NOTICE.md now copies the merged
  NOTICE.md, as tools/check-agent-plugin-manifest.py requires, and the
  clause of its Scope section on the paths in the Site template
  section, which now names none, is removed from both files.
- Add .github/squash/269.txt with this squash message for the
  Pull request text workflow.
